messages:
Sam: Heads up — Tier-2 customer (AcmeMaps) opened an escalation: recurring 429s and their telemetry shows retries doubled their bill. Started ~2026-03-05T15:12:10Z after the config rollout.

Sam: Root error in our logs: \u201Crate_limiter: 429 quota_exhausted client_id=acme-123\u201D. They claim no traffic change on their end; pattern is short bursts (~10s) of high QPS.

Priya: I'm taking this. Can you paste the exact request headers / sample request they were sending? Any client-id or tenant header?

Sam: Example they provided:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \\n  -H 'X-Client-Id: acme-123' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"input":"some prompt"}'
```
They were firing ~40-60 req/s in bursts lasting 8-12s, then idle. Retries kicked in and made it worse.

Miguel: tagging in rate-limiter owner. I pulled the limiter configs that rolled at 2026-03-05T15:05:03Z — there's a suspect change to the refill math. Looks like window units were interpreted as ms instead of s after the templating tweak.

Miguel: Repro locally in canary: bump burst_size to 500 and set refill_window=100 (intended to be seconds but now treated as ms). Limiter logs show:
```
2026-03-05T15:11:58Z limiter: client=acme-123 tokens=0 limit=100 refill=1/100ms issued=429
2026-03-05T15:12:01Z limiter: client=acme-123 tokens=0 issued=429
```
Clients hit 429s even when under expected sustainable QPS.

Jordan: Rolling back limiter config to v2.7.1 across prod-pool-3 now. Running:`kubectl apply -f limiter-config-v2.7.1.yaml` and restarting pods gradually.

Ava: Notifying AcmeMaps with a holding msg: "we're investigating, temporary mitigation applied (quota bump)". Support is offering a temporary +200 quota for 1 hour while we investigate.

Sam: After rollback the customer confirms 429s stopped and retries subsided. They reported transient latency increases but no further 429s.

Priya: Thanks. Miguel — can you open a fix PR and include unit/regression tests for unit conversion? Also we need a stronger canary gate for config templating changes.

Miguel: PR 4826 opened: fix is in limiter/refill.go — explicit unit parse and validation plus a regression test that simulates 10s bursts. Link: https://git.redwood/infer/pull/4826

Jordan: Deploying patch to canary now. Running a scripted load test:
```
artillery quick --count 5 -n 200 'https://canary.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \\n  --headers 'X-Client-Id: acme-123'
```
Early results look good — no unexpected 429s under the burst profile.

Priya: Post-incident action items (we agreed in-thread):
1) Add metric/alert for refill_window anomalies and unit mismatch warnings.
2) Canary test that generates 5-15s bursts across >100 client-ids.
3) Add runbook steps: exact rollback command, how to perform emergency quota bump, and contact matrix.
4) Add a billing safeguard: do not auto-retry billing-affecting requests more than N times; surface to support.
5) Update templating validation to reject ambiguous unit fields.

Sam: Finance flagged this as billing-impacting — customer was charged for retry traffic. @FinanceBot can you provision a provisional credit while postmortem completes?

FinanceBot: Provisional credit approved: $500 (pending postmortem).

Miguel: Additional mitigation I'm proposing: add a lightweight client-level circuit breaker that returns 503 after repeated 429s for a short cooldown to avoid billing loops. I'll open PR 4830 for that.

Ava: I'll coordinate customer success follow-up and confirm credit applied. Also will draft the customer-facing explanation with non-technical wording and timeline.

Priya: Incident resolved for now — rollback fixed prod. We'll schedule a 30-min postmortem tomorrow and assign owners for the action items. I'll create the postmortem doc and link it here once done.

Sam: Thanks everyone, great triage and quick rollback. Marking this thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
